approach: Add a family check to Config::validate (crates/athena-data/src/config.rs:639), after the hard_producer_model check at :670-674. Config::parse calls validate on every load (:616-619). The check matches case-insensitively on the substrings opus, sonnet and haiku across reader, producer_default, producer_allowed, verifier and hard_producer_model. A missing family returns a new ConfigError::ModelFamily(&'static str). Its message says the rule applies to every athena.toml Athena loads and how to satisfy it. config.rs unit tests remove each family from REPO_CONFIG text and assert the exact error. A new integration test, crates/athena-core/tests/model_roster.rs, parses the repository athena.toml through the real loader. It asserts the roles cover all three families, that a haiku-less copy is refused, that OLY-B-SET-02 in docs/spec.toml no longer has mechanism none, and the existing jev::ENDPOINT and jev::MODEL constants. jev.rs, lib.rs, athena.toml, defaults.toml and the workflows are untouched. docs/spec.toml gets a real mechanism and a measure ending `status: not shown`. xtask/shard-timings.txt gets the new test line. CHANGELOG.md gets an entry. briefs.rs is a no-change check (see Files). The history walk (`athena check --history`) is added to the dependents with evidence and a named check.

decisions.choice: Enforce the roles in Config::validate with ConfigError::ModelFamily(&'static str), matching lowercase substrings on reader, producer_default, producer_allowed, verifier and hard_producer_model. The message states that it applies to every athena.toml Athena loads and says how to satisfy it. The CHANGELOG entry says the same (finding 3).
decisions.reason: validate is the one non-test reader every load reaches: Config::parse (config.rs:616), config_at (athena-gate/src/lib.rs:178-192), JobConfig::at (capability.rs:41), admission (admission.rs:933) and the user-repository load (athena-cli/src/wiring.rs:206). The rule is deliberately global, because the requirement (BRIEF.md:25) is Athena's own model set and any config Athena runs must keep it. No model-id list is needed, so a version bump such as claude-opus-5-6 keeps passing.

decisions.choice: Cover the history walk with evidence (option a of finding 1) and name the CI history job as the check that must pass. Add no athena-gate test.
decisions.reason: check_history_with_exempt (athena-gate/src/history.rs:235-243) calls Judged::new for every commit, and Judged::new (lib.rs:291-299) runs config_at on the first parent. A config that now fails validate becomes a Rule::Configuration violation for that commit. check_legacy (legacy.rs:165) reuses this walk, and CI runs `athena check --history` (.github/workflows/ci.yml:606-607). Evidence that past configs held all three families: docs/decisions.md:325-327 and :725-726 record the Haiku/Sonnet producers and the Opus verifier from v0. validate has always required the verifier to be outside producer_allowed and the default producer to be inside it (config.rs:643-656), so any config that parsed had an Opus-class verifier and a Sonnet/Haiku producer set. The family match is a substring, so version bumps do not matter. Only a past commit that used a non-family alias would fail, and the CI history job is the check that sees it. A new athena-gate test would touch files outside the deliverables list.

risks.risk: A past athena.toml in the history may lack a family by name, and `athena check --history` would then report a Configuration violation for that commit (history.rs:239-242). HISTORY.txt lists paths, not contents, so I could not check old file text.
risks.mitigation: The v0 decisions (docs/decisions.md:325-327, :725-726) and the old validate rules (config.rs:643-656) imply Opus, Sonnet and Haiku were always present. The family match is a substring. The CI job `athena check --history` (ci.yml:606-607) and `cargo test -p athena-gate` are named as the checks that must pass. If the history job fails on an old commit, the producer reports it and does not weaken the rule silently.

risks.risk: A future model alias without opus, sonnet or haiku in its name would be refused.
risks.mitigation: The error names the family and says how to satisfy the rule. The match is case-insensitive substring, so version bumps and vendor prefixes pass. An alias change needs a deliberate edit of the rule.

risks.risk: A text-replacement test passes for the wrong reason if the pattern misses or another error fires first.
risks.mitigation: The helper asserts the text changed. Each case asserts the exact ModelFamily variant and family. The opus case uses a verifier outside producer_allowed, so VerifierCanProduce cannot fire first.

risks.risk: Comments that describe the Jev constants use an HTTP-client word and fail external_calls_guard.
risks.mitigation: Step 2 and step 4 forbid those words, and external_calls_guard is in the producer's check list.

risks.risk: The spec slice test in model_roster.rs depends on the layout of docs/spec.toml (`id =` followed by the next `[[requirement]]`).
risks.mitigation: It slices on the id line and the next `[[requirement]]` header, the same layout as the entries at :2019-2026. Using the first match only keeps it simple, and it panics with a readable message if the id is not found.

risks.risk: The 5.00 s timing for the new shard unit is a guess.
risks.mitigation: The file header already marks the values as estimates; the new value is labelled as an estimate in the CHANGELOG.

demonstrations.method: New unit tests in the config.rs tests module (it imports super::*, and REPO_CONFIG = include_str!(athena.toml) at config.rs:888). A helper applies (from, to) replacen edits to REPO_CONFIG and asserts the text changed, so a pattern that misses cannot pass silently. Each case asserts matches!(Config::parse(&text), Err(ConfigError::ModelFamily("haiku" | "sonnet" | "opus"))) with the exact family and that the message names the family and says the rule applies to every athena.toml. Controls: the unchanged REPO_CONFIG parses, and uppercase names such as Claude-Haiku still count.

demonstrations.seam: The entry points are the cargo commands. The ci_shards oracle lists targets from the crates' tests/ directories, so the new file is picked up automatically. The seam exists.

demonstrations.method: Read CHANGELOG.md and confirm a new entry under [Unreleased] / Added, in the style of the entries at CHANGELOG.md:12-20. It must say that OLY-B-SET-02 now has a mechanism, that Config::validate refuses a [models] section whose roles lack an Opus, a Sonnet or a Haiku model for every athena.toml Athena loads, name the tests, and say Jev stays shadow-only. Run `git diff --stat` and `git status`. They show no change to athena.toml, defaults.toml, .github/workflows, jev.rs or lib.rs. The policy test runs the boundary-word and personal-data scan.
demonstrations.observes: The policy scan passes. The diff lists docs/spec.toml, crates/athena-data/src/config.rs, crates/athena-core/tests/model_roster.rs, CHANGELOG.md and xtask/shard-timings.txt. crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs is deliberately absent (see Files).
demonstrations.fails_without: The changelog read fails if the entry is missing. The policy test fails if an email-like string or a banned word is added.
demonstrations.seam: The entry points are a file read, git diff and the xtask policy test. No fake. The seam exists.
